description:
Create an identity to issue documents as: the seller side.

`legal_name`, `tax_id`, address and bank details are what appears as the
issuer, and what an e-invoicing ruleset checks. Distinct from a branding
profile, which sets colours and a logo and says nothing about who you are.

ElectronicAddress.description:
BT-34 / BT-49 — where a document is routed on Peppol or DBNA.

Both halves are required: an identifier without its scheme cannot be
resolved, because the same string means different things in different code
lists. This is not the tax id, which identifies a company to a tax
authority rather than a mailbox on a network.

scheme_id.description: EAS code list identifier — 0088 is GLN, 9930 a German VAT number.
scheme_id.title: Scheme Id

ElectronicAddress.title: ElectronicAddress

bank_account.description: Where to send the money. Becomes the invoice's payment instructions (BG-16) unless a document states an account of its own; some national rulesets require them.

contact_name.description: Who to ask about an invoice — a person or a department, not the company. EN 16931 calls it the contact point (BT-41 for the seller, BT-56 for the buyer); some national rulesets require it.
contact_name.title: Contact Name

electronic_address.description: Network address for e-invoicing. Required by Peppol; not the tax id.
